back: An importer's order for goods from abroad; open (agent chooses supplier) or closed (supplier named).
Sea freight: receipt for goods, contract of carriage and document of title.
Air freight: receipt and contract of carriage; not a document of title.
Invoice certified by the importing country's consul to confirm the value of goods.
States where goods were made; used for preferential duty and trade restrictions.
Importer's bank promises to pay the exporter on presentation of the shipping documents.
Order to pay a stated sum on demand or at a future date; can be discounted at a bank.
Collect duties, prevent smuggling, enforce restrictions, control bonded warehouses, collect trade statistics.
Customs-controlled store where imported goods wait without paying duty until released for home use or re-exported.
